articles.title: A Pragmatic Uptime and Deployment Guide for Early-Stage Startups
articles.excerpt: Early-stage startups often fall into one of two extremes when building infrastructure. Either they spend months over-engineering a complex Kubernetes cluster for an application with 50 users, or they…
articles.body: Early-stage startups often fall into one of two extremes when building infrastructure. Either they spend months over-engineering a complex Kubernetes cluster for an application with 50 users, or they run everything on a single, fragile virtual machine with zero automated backups and no monitoring. Both approaches lead to the same result: a 3 AM wake-up call when a container crashes, a disk fills up, or a bad deployment breaks the production database. As a founder or technical lead, your goal is not to chase five-nines of availability on day one. Your goal is to build a backend foundation that is boring, predictable, and doesn't demand midnight firefighting.

articles.title: Why do time tracker extensions need permission to read every tab you open? I built an offline AI one that doesn't.
articles.excerpt: Install almost any popular time-tracking extension from the Chrome Web Store and look at the permission popup: "Read and change all your data on all websites." Why? Because most of them inject content…
articles.body: Install almost any popular time-tracking extension from the Chrome Web Store and look at the permission popup: "Read and change all your data on all websites." Why? Because most of them inject content scripts into Jira, GitHub, Linear, and half the internet just to render a tiny "Start Timer" button next to your ticket titles. Those injected buttons slow down heavy web apps, randomly break every time Atlassian or GitHub ships a frontend tweak, and require blanket access to tabs that have nothing to do with your work. And even after all that bloat, half of us still end up staring at our git commits and Slack threads at 5 PM trying to reconstruct what we did at 10 AM.

articles.excerpt: My project has zero GitHub stars. Not "a few". Zero. And last week, an international developer-tools site featured it — with my name and my city in the credit line — without me ever submitting it. No…
articles.body: My project has zero GitHub stars . Not "a few". Zero. And last week, an international developer-tools site featured it — with my name and my city in the credit line — without me ever submitting it. No form. No email. No "please consider my project." They found it on their own. This is the story of how that happened, what I built, and the three things zero stars taught me about getting discovered. 👋 First, Who Am I? I'm Ali Ahmad, a student from Lahore, Pakistan . I attend college during the day and build software at night — usually between 10 p.m. and 3 a.m., which is when most of this story happened. I'm not backed by anyone. There's no team, no funding, no audience. For months, my total distribution strategy was: build the thing properly, and hope. Hope is not a strategy.

articles.body: Explore This Section Science Citizen Science Amateur Astronomer? Be a… Overview Resources Opportunities Citizen Science Highlights About Science Activation Neutron stars are the ultra-dense, city-sized leftovers of dead stars. When they collide, they can release a brief flash of light called a kilonova . These immensely powerful events forge much of the universe’s gold, platinum and other heavy elements. Since a kilonova fades within days, astronomers have to find it fast, and no single observatory can watch the whole sky. But if you have a telescope with a camera, or access to one, you can help find and follow these cosmic fireworks as a part of NASA’s Kilonova Catcher project! Kilonova Catcher connects amateur astronomers around the world into a rapid-response network.

articles.body: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25, will deliver about 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. The mission will be the third flight of the company’s Cygnus XL, the larger, more cargo-capable version of the company’s solar-powered spacecraft. The Cygnus XL will launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Following arrival to the station, astronauts aboard the space station will use the Canadarm2 to grapple the spacecraft before ground controllers robotically install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading.

articles.title: 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death
articles.excerpt: Astronomers have caught a rare transitional phase at the end of a star's life, a fossilized remnant of stellar death throes, that could change our picture of the sun's final days.
articles.body: As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed.

articles.title: Raising the stakes for enterprise networks with AI modernization
articles.excerpt: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network. Now, agentic AI is add…
articles.body: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network . Now, agentic AI is adding to the load. Tasks conducted by AI agents generate an estimated 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by human workers. As AI inference shifts from hyperscale training clouds—the huge centralized data centers where raw AI models ingest vast datasets and learn—to real-time, latency-sensitive applications, the need for on-premises or near-premises infrastructure grows. As a result, the gap between enterprise networks that are ready to support AI and those that are not is widening.
